title: Senior Business Intelligence Lead (all genders)
description:
Your Mission

EV charging is evolving from a niche technology into everyday infrastructure. As reev grows, teams increasingly need reliable, consistently defined metrics. Today, different dashboards, reporting dates, filters, and assumptions can produce different answers to the same business question. 
This role addresses the problem - not by building more dashboards, but by creating a shared and trustworthy data foundation. The goal is to establish clear definitions and consistent metrics so that teams and leadership can make informed decisions based on the same numbers. Someone who understands that unclear definitions, rather than a lack of data, are often the real problem can make a significant impact in this role. You own the certified layer, the single, agreed upon version of every core metric that reev runs on. You connect the definition, the data model, and the delivery. And when two numbers disagree, you are the person who says which one to trust. 

What you will do 

  • Define core metrics with Finance, Product, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Engineering, and Platform.
  • Agree on definitions, data contracts, and ownership forcore metrics with the teams that own them.
  • Maintain and verify the certified data layer, built in ETL tooland surfaced in Metabase, so teams can build their own dashboards on top of it.
  • Use SQL to validate data, investigate inconsistencies, and trace numbers back to their sources.
  • Work with Platform team to identify potential improvements in data flows, pipelines, and transformations, advise on next steps, and help prioritize next steps during planning.

title: Senior Python Engineer, Platform Libraries (m/f/d)
description:
The role

We’re looking for a Senior Python Engineer, Platform Libraries (m/f/d) to join our team and play a key role in developing software that connects and translates lab equipment hardware interfaces, automates machines, and powers our next-generation automation platform. As a core team member, you will be working on cutting-edge technology, building software that bridges the gap between software and hardware, enabling seamless integration across various vendors.

Connectors are how we do it. Every instrument we bring online gets one, and every connector is built on our shared Python libraries: Bus, our Connector Development Kit, and the stack underneath them.

Our mission is to empower researchers and engineers by bridging the gap between lab equipment and cloud-based automation. Our customers are solving critical challenges like curing diseases, developing sustainable materials, and addressing global food security. We provide them with the tools to connect their devices, automate workflows, and unlock new possibilities in R&D.

Your mandate has two halves. Own the libraries as a product with real users, our own engineers today and external contributors later. And stay close enough to customer connector work that what you build is grounded in problems that actually exist.


Why you'll love this role

Your users are engineers. Your success lets other people ship connectors faster. That's a different craft from shipping features, and it's the one we're hiring for.

Real hardware, real failure modes. Instruments time out, return garbage, and arrive with documentation that's wrong. You'll debug against physical devices in our Munich workshop.


Open source on purpose. Our CDK and our standardization work (SiLA 2) are public. What you build gets used and criticized by people outside the company.


Senior scope, small team. You'll be the person who decides how connector engineering works here. No layer between you and that decision.


Your mission

1. The Builder: own the shared libraries

  • Own Bus, the CDK, and the core stack. Features, tests, CI, releases, and deprecations across the connectors already running in production.

  • Extract abstractions from real work. When the same pattern shows up in the third connector, it becomes a library feature. You're the one who notices, and the one who does it.

  • Make the docs good enough to remove yourself. An outside contributor should be able to build a connector on our libraries without a call.

  • Set the quality standard. You define what "tested" means before a connector reaches a customer, and you make it stick.

2. The Shipper: build connectors on real instruments

  • Ship production connectors end to end. Spec sheet, physical device, protocol, proof of connectivity, tested connector, live customer. Independently.

  • Reverse-engineer what isn't documented. Roughly half the instruments we touch have incomplete or wrong docs. Packet captures, trial and error, vendor calls.

  • Work with the workshop. Our Connector Factory team gets instruments development-ready. You take it from there.

  • Talk to the people who use it. Automation engineers and scientists at biotech and pharma customers. Their constraints shape what the libraries need next.


Your profile

  • Deep Python: 5+ years of writing production Python other people depend on. Async, typing, packaging, testing. You've designed APIs that other engineers built on, not just glue code.

  • You've debugged a real protocol against real hardware: gRPC, serial, TCP, OPC UA, CAN, USB. Which one matters less than having sat with a packet capture and a device that won't respond.

  • You ship without a spec: When the documentation is wrong, you reverse-engineer, instead of filing a vendor ticket and waiting. 

  • You build for other developers: An SDK, a library, an internal platform. Something where your job was making other engineers faster.

  • Located in Munich: The instruments are physically here at WERK1. 


Nice to have

  • SiLA 2, or another device abstraction and interoperability standard

  • Lab automation, scientific instruments, or a life science background

  • Open source maintainership with actual external contributors

  • C, C++, .NET, or Rust, for the vendor DLLs and drivers we end up wrapping

  • Docker, Kubernetes, edge deployment

  • German, for vendor conversations


Probably not a fit if

Better to say this now than in week 6.


  • Your Python is all APIs and databases and you've never debugged a physical device.

  • You'd want two quarters to redesign the library architecture before shipping a connector.

  • You like shipping integrations but have no appetite for going back afterwards to generalise, test, and document.

  • You want the library work without the customer deadlines. Both are in the job.


About UniteLabs

UniteLabs is on the mission to accelerate scientific progress by automating lab processes with scalable infrastructure.

We’re a startup based in Munich, Germany, pioneering an industry-first integration platform for lab automation, bridging hardware and software across vendor barriers to revolutionize life science R&D. By digitalizing life science R&D, we enable researchers in biotech, pharma, chemistry, and food industries to accelerate their work in groundbreaking fields such as disease treatment, sustainable materials, and food security.

Our platform empowers customers to analyze more data, run autonomous experiments, and leverage AI-driven solutions, driving innovation and efficiency. At UniteLabs, we are committed to providing the infrastructure that powers the future of scientific discovery.

As one of the first full-time hires, you'll thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and take on significant responsibilities from day one. We are a tech-driven company that takes pride in our solutions—and we’re looking for individuals who share that passion and want to grow with the company into leadership and expert roles.


Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Impactful Work: Work on meaningful products in an ambitious, supportive environment as part of a team revolutionizing connectivity in laboratory automation to enable breakthroughs in science and technology.

  • Work with the Best: Join a talented, ambitious team in a dynamic, transparent environment where your ideas help shape the company's future.

  • Collaborative Culture: Team-oriented environment focused on continuous knowledge-sharing and professional growth, with regular team-building activities including offsites and work-cations.

  • Flexible Environment: Backed by an employee-first culture that supports flexible remote work and PTO, with our main office in the vibrant WERK1 Munich hub. Hardware debugging happens there, so being regularly onsite is a must.

  • Attractive Compensation Package: Competitive compensation with growth potential in a VC-backed startup, along with a laptop of choice, annual productivity budget, and a growing list of benefits for sports, mobility, insurance, and more.


Tech stack

A non-exhaustive list of our main technologies and tools used for a given task:

  • Connectors: Python, SiLA 2, gRPC, zeroconf

  • Workflows: Python, Prefect

  • Services: TypeScript, NestJS, Prisma

  • Web: TypeScript, Vue 3, Nuxt 3, TailwindCSS

  • Cloud: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, AWS, Terraform

  • Databases: PostgreSQL


How to apply

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
⭐️ Your Impact:

The European trades are one of the least digitised industries left. Software
penetration sits under 15%, against roughly 70% in the US. The labour
productivity gap runs about 30%. Millions of skilled people spend their evenings
on paperwork instead of the craft they trained for — in the industry that has to
deliver the energy transition.

There is almost no incumbent software to displace. That is unusual, and it won't
last.

smalt replaces the back office entirely rather than selling Meister another tool
to manage. In the last six months that went from a partner app and a dashboard
to around thirty AI agents in production - pricing real jobs, qualifying real
leads, running the operations of businesses whose payroll depends on it working.

These days building thirty agents is easy. Knowing which thirty is what's challenging.

That only comes from being in the Betrieb and talking to the Handwerker.

That's what this role is for.

What you'll do

You'll sit in Handwerksbetrieben - at the Meister's desk, in the van, on site, next to our team -
and watch how the work actually happens. Then you'll come back and build the
thing that fixes it, often multiple times on the same day.

- Spend real time with partners. Not a quarterly customer call. You'll know
  our Meister by name, understand their P&L, and notice the thing they've
  stopped complaining about because they assume it can't be fixed.
- Build across the stack. Python/FastAPI services, Vue interfaces, Flutter
  screens, agent loops, data pipelines - whatever the problem needs.
- Own agents in production. Not demos. Agents that price real jobs, answer
  real customers, and cost real money when they're wrong. Reliability,
  evaluation, structured output, graceful failure.
- Decide what to build. You'll write your own acceptance criteria. Nobody
  here will hand you a spec, and waiting for one is how to fail in this
  role.
- Measure whether it worked. Hours saved per partner, offers that go out
  untouched, leads answered before a competitor picks up. If the number didn't
  move, it didn't work.

What that looks like in practice

In July one of our Meister got an early build of the partner app, ahead of the
general rollout. He tested it between jobs and sent screenshots: from a calendar
appointment he could no longer jump into the project to pull the customer's
phone number. He had a reply in two minutes. Within the hour he'd also asked for
a navigation button - tap the address, go straight to maps.

Neither was news. Both were already being worked on before he hit send.

We aim to be fast, and close enough to the work that we've usually seen the problem before the person living it has to tell us.



✨ What Makes You a Great Fit:

You might be a great fit if you

- Have owned something end to end - architecture through delivery through the
  unglamorous iteration afterwards. We don't count years; we look at what you
  carried.
- Get obsessed with a problem rather than a stack. The tools change every few
  months. The curiosity compounds.
- Would rather ship something that changes a tradesperson's week than win an
  argument about abstractions.
- Actually like talking to customers, and have changed your mind about a feature
  because of something a user said.
- Are comfortable being the least knowledgeable person in a room full of
  electricians, and ask the question anyway.
- Can hold "ship it today" and "this needs to survive two years" in your head at
  the same time, and know which one applies.

Our stack, so you know what you're walking into:

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL (with pgvector), Celery, Redis
- Frontend: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite, PrimeVue
- Mobile: Flutter
- AI: Anthropic, Open source and Google models, vector search over partner and catalog data
- Infra: Google Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Sentry

We care that you're strong somewhere and unafraid everywhere else. If you've
never written Vue but you've shipped production systems and you learn fast, that
is fine - several of us hadn't either.

What we do look for:

- Production experience with LLM-powered features, and the scars that come with it: evaluation, structured output parsing, context management, error recovery
- A track record of shipping things people actually used
- High agency. You'll get context and constraints, not instructions.
- Raw intelligence paired with a humble mindset

German is helpful and you'll pick some up either way - our partners speak it all day. It isn't a requirement but definitely a nice to have. The the team works in English.

- Real ownership, and direct proximity to the founders - and to General
  Catalyst, noa, Owl Ventures and Heartfelt

title: Senior Product Engineer (DevTools & AI reliability, remote)
description:
(Fully remote, async-first, DevTools SaaS, 32-40h/week, time zones: UTC-3 to UTC+3)

The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.

They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: end-to-end tests and synthetic monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.

Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel.

Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. You will build reliability for this kind of software.

Our stack is AI (Codex, Claude, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Golang, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We ship to prod all day, every day. We practice Agile (not scrum) and take pride in good documentation and good looking products.

We’re a remote-first startup that keeps things simple—low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love building cool things, working async, actually listening to and working with customers, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!

What you'll do

Build and ship with AI

You will actively use coding agents for full stack development, from exploring solutions and generating scaffolding to refactoring, test generation and debugging. At Checkly we push the limits of AI tools every day.

Talk to our users

You will talk directly to the developers, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams who are on-call, debugging incidents, or wiring Checkly into production pipelines. You will understand their workflows, pain points, and feedback. You use those conversations to validate ideas, course-correct early, and iterate on what you build. Customer calls and the weekly support rotation are part of the job, not a distraction from it.

Find the right problems to solve

In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will focus on real developer pain: flaky tests and flaky checks, unclear failures, noisy alerts. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements.

Own your work end to end

From shaping the initial idea, through implementation and rollout, to watching how it behaves in production. You will take part in on-call and help support customers when things don’t work as expected.

What you should have

  • You have shipped features with AI, not just experimented with them. You have taken work from zero to shipped with a comparable stack, made implementation decisions that held up, and put things in front of real users.

  • You have built and run production software. You know the realities of operating software that people depend on: edge cases, incidents, regressions, and the need for observability and follow-up. You are not surprised when things break. You help fix them.

  • You can hold a product conversation, not just a technical one. You can look at a customer problem and reason about whether the thing we are about to build actually solves it.

  • You work well without an office around you. You are autonomous and self-motivated in a remote setup, and you still enjoy getting to know your colleagues and helping other people get unstuck.

  • FULLY remote role, within the UTC-3 to UTC+3 time zones. You need to be able to travel to (other) European countries without having to wait for a visa appointment, for our annual kickoff, a team meetup or a conference.

What you will hate about us

We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.

  • We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.

  • We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.

  • We are lean, so you own the unglamorous parts too. There is no separate QA team, no ops layer to hand things off to, and you are on the support rotation and the on-call rotation like everyone else.

  • We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.

  • Customer signals come first, and most of the time they matter more than your instinct. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up.

Benefits

  • Become part of a fast-growing, international, and remote team where your work matters, and your impact won't get lost in layers of bureaucracy.

title: Climate Asset Development Lead (f/d/m)
description:
A definitive shift is currently happening. Corporates across the globe are no longer just reporting on sustainability; they are actively investing in it as a core financial and strategic asset.

At CEEZER, we are architecting the infrastructure for enterprise-grade Climate Performance Asset management, transforming how the world's largest companies source and manage carbon credits, Energy Attribution Certificates (EAC), and Sustainable Aviation Fuel certificates (SAFc).

Our platform gives the world’s most ambitious enterprises the data-driven precision, real-time monitoring, and framework-compliant reporting required to confidently deploy capital toward high-impact Climate Performance Asset portfolios and true, measurable climate action.

We are looking for a Climate Asset Development Lead (f/d/m), You will lead CEEZER’s expansion into climate performance assets by owning our strategy and deal execution across EAC, SAFc, and the secondary carbon market. Starting as a team of one, you'll drive supply origination, provide market expertise to clients, and scale your team alongside business growth.


Your mission

  • Setting up the strategy for climate performance asset supply access across EAC, SAFc, and the secondary carbon market.

  • Evaluate and end-to-end drive the expansion of CEEZER in new climate performance assets, from market assessment to transaction.

  • Run the trading of climate performance assets: Ensure supply access, execute deals hands-on, negotiate prices & contracts, and structure complex transactions.

  • Lead and grow the Climate Asset Development team, starting with our Climate Asset Trader, setting priorities and building the team as volume grows.

  • Establish CEEZER's thought leadership on EAC and SAFc, provide expert insights and ensure the latest policy and market trends translate into strategy and execution company-wide.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, registries, and regulatory bodies and act as our subject-matter expert in client conversations.

  • Drive company-wide projects and collaborate closely with key stakeholders across Revenue, Supply, Operations, and Product.

  • Collect and structure data, collect quotes, and collaborate with data platforms and intelligence providers as a basis for analyses, forecasts, and decision-making.

What you need to succeed

  • 4+ years of experience in strategy consulting, VC-backed startups, or similar high-performance environments. Experience with any climate performance assets, trading, or energy markets is a plus.

  • Exceptional analytical skill set with attention to detail.

  • Executional excellence balanced with speed, and comfort taking measured risks within a defined framework.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills, strong in building relationships with heterogeneous stakeholders internally and externally. Leadership experience is a plus.

  • High ownership, accountability, and integrity, paired with willingness to learn and grow.

  • Strong business acumen and commercial hunger.

  • Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree in business, economics, finance, international relations, environmental studies or a related field is a plus.

  • Fluency in English is required.

  • A valid work permit in Germany.

The hiring process

  • An intro call with the People Team.

  • A call with our SVP Sourcing & Delivery, Stephan.

  • A call with our Climate Asset Trader, Pietro.

  • A deep-dive case study with our SVP Sourcing & Delivery and additional stakeholders.

What's in it for you at CEEZER?

  • A mission that matters: Work alongside international teams combining finance, tech, and climate science professionals to direct capital toward the world's most critical climate assets.

  • Accelerated growth: We are scaling fast, and your career will too. Take opportunities to lead cross-functional initiatives and expand your strategic influence.

  • True ownership: We are building in a brand-new market, meaning many of our best practices don’t exist yet. If you see a better workflow, tool, or strategy, you have the autonomy and backing to build it.

  • An empowering environment: We bring together diverse global perspectives, knowing that solving complex climate challenges requires a wide mix of backgrounds and expertise.

  • Real enterprise impact: Transform how global corporates approach sustainability. CEEZER hosts 50Mt+ of vetted carbon credits across all pathways, all backed by sophisticated data and institutional-grade risk management.

  • A net-zero career: We practice what we preach. From your first day, we fully offset your personal and professional carbon footprint because sustainability is how we operate.

 

Create an impact with us

We know that great talent doesn’t always follow a linear path. If your experience doesn't check every single box on this list, but you have the drive and unique strengths to excel here, we still want to hear from you.

Here, building a diverse team isn't a checkbox—It’s how we solve complex global challenges. We make all hiring decisions based on merit, skills, and potential, while actively working to keep unconscious bias out of our process. We’ve created an environment where all individuals feel valued and empowered to succeed. We welcome diverse applicants and are dedicated to providing equal opportunities for everyone to thrive.

If you need any adjustments or specific accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know. We are here to support you.

About us

CEEZER is the leading partner for Climate Performance Asset procurement and management, empowering businesses to transform climate ambition into a clear path to net-zero. Trusted by major organizations including Deutsche Telekom, LGT, and Nasdaq, CEEZER provides the confidence needed to implement effective climate action strategies. For more information, visit ceezer.earth.

Kaum jemand kennt den Praxisalltag so gut wie jemand, der ihn selbst erlebt hat. Experience: 2+ years as a QA engineer

Welcome to Miaplaza!

Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive homeschool curriculum platform where all students can be successful! Our K-8 platforms include Miacademy, Always Icecream, and Clever Dragons, and our 9-12 options include MiaPrep and MiaPrep Online High School. Our student base is rapidly growing, and we’re hiring for multiple positions across several departments! Our expansion stems from our commitment to providing exceptional educational content and our pursuit of new opportunities. 🚀

▶️ You can hear our CEO, Johannes Ziegler, discuss our company’s values and future!

How you’ll make an impact (position summary):

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!

The Role

We're looking for a QA Engineer to join our current QA team. You'll take ownership of how we test, validate, and sign off on quality across our platform. We're actively investing in our QA practice: expanding automated test coverage, improving our release testing process, and moving toward a model where quality is embedded throughout the development lifecycle.

You'll report to a technical Engineering Manager and work alongside engineers who value clear test documentation, reliable automation, and confident code releases.

As a mature company, we have legacy systems and established manual testing workflows, but we are transitioning to modern automated testing practices using Playwright and TypeScript. The split between manual and automated work varies, but you should be comfortable working across both, bringing automation where it adds the most value while pragmatically maintaining manual coverage where it's still the right tool.

A core goal of our QA evolution is to make testing faster, more reliable, and less dependent on last-minute changes before each release: replacing fragile manual regression cycles with stable automated suites, reducing flakiness, and building coverage that the whole team can rely on. Every testing investment is measured by whether it improves quality and reduces the team's burden at release time.

What You'll Do

  • Write and maintain automated regression tests; review automation MRs from peers

  • Execute manual testing across web UIs (functional, regression, cross-platform, responsive layouts on mobile/tablet)

  • Create and maintain test cases, checklists, and test documentation in TestRail

  • File clear, actionable bug reports with reproduction steps; collaborate with developers to triage and resolve

  • Own the release testing process to ensure only high-quality changes ship

  • Partner with PMs and designers on requirements review, edge cases, and acceptance criteria

  • Contribute to QA process improvements as we scale (currently a 2-person team growing to 4)

How We Work

We believe you should know what your days look like before you accept an offer.

We don't have much bureaucracy. Small team, direct communication, short decision loops. If you've worked at places where opening a Jira ticket to request a Jira ticket was normal, this isn't that. Here's the reality:

Meetings (yes, we keep them minimal):

  • Daily standup with your product team. Show up, share updates and unblock each other..

  • Sprint planning and retrospectives with your product team, once per sprint.

  • 1:1 with your Engineering Manager - Regular cadence, your agenda.

  • Monthly Engineering all-hands.

  • That's it. The rest of your time is yours to work.

Deployments:

  • Bi-monthly release cadence with a schedule published in advance. As a QA Engineer, you own the release testing window. Coordinating with developers, running regression suites, and signing off on quality before the release.

  • Infrequent ad-hoc hotfixes

Communication:

  • Async-friendly. Documentation-first.

  • Slack/ Jira/ GitLab MRs/ Notion

  • Google Workspace for email and documents.

  • Zoom for video calls.

Timezone:

  • We need significant overlap with typical CET (Central European Time) working hours to coordinate and collaborate synchronously. Additionally we have stakeholders and developers in US timezones that we occasionally need to meet.


What We're Looking For

Requirements (Requisite Skills): 

  • 2+ years of QA engineering experience, including web UI testing

  • 2+ years of experience with Playwright or a similar test automation framework (e.g. Cypress, Selenium, Puppeteer)

  • 2+ years of experience using TypeScript

  • Strong test design skills: comfortable writing and maintaining test cases, checklists, and test documentation

  • Familiarity with QA's role in the SDLC and how to collaborate with developers and PMs

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail

  • Upper-intermediate English (B2+) for written and spoken communication

  • Strong experience in manual testing and writing manual test cases

Nice to have:

  • Experience with accessibility and/or security testing

How you’ll work with other teams:

Career Growth

We have a defined career ladder. Whether your path leads toward Senior/Staff QA Engineer or Engineering Management, there's room to grow - and we'll work with you to get there.

Onboarding

Every team member gets full support throughout onboarding, and no one expects you to figure out the ins and outs on your own. We'll pair with you, answer every question, and make sure you have the context you need. New hires typically feel very supported at Miaplaza.

What success looks like here: In the first couple of months, you're asking a lot of clarifying questions, reading documentation, exploring the product independently, and writing and running tests with confidence. By months 3-4, you're taking ownership of a specific area, building out test coverage, identifying gaps, and driving quality improvements. By month 5-6, you're contributing meaningfully to the testing strategy for migration and modernisation work and operating independently. The common thread: curiosity, initiative, and the habit of investigating before you ask, but always asking when you need to.

Interview Process

Our process is staged and designed to respect your time. Expect a mix of introductory conversation, technical discussion, and practical evaluation. We want to understand how you think about real problems and testing practices. As part of the process, we will ask for professional references and conduct a background check in accordance with applicable law. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, let us know, we're happy to help.

Compensation

Competitive compensation, open to negotiation based on your experience and expertise. We'll discuss specifics early in the process so neither side wastes time. Since we’re remote-first, every arrangement is different; we tailor time off, benefits, and perks as part of your individual contract to ensure the overall package works for both sides.

Ready to apply?

Join our team at Miaplaza! Start by submitting your application and resume. Our hiring process involves a screening call, followed by a behavioral interview, and two technical interviews.

title: Robotics Software Engineer Intern – Swarm Systems (m/f/d)
description:

  • Analyze simulation and field-test data to identify issues and opportunities for improvement
  • Contribute to the core robotics stack in areas such as estimation, perception, planning, control, or mission execution
  • Collaborate closely with robotics, simulation, embedded, and domain experts
  • Gain practical experience developing and validating software for complex autonomous systems


Your profile

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master's degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Autonomous Systems, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
  • Good programming skills in C++, ideally modern C++ (17/20)
  • Solid foundation in algorithms, data structures, and software engineering
  • Basic understanding of robotics concepts such as coordinate frames, sensor data, estimation, planning, or control
  • Comfortable working in Linux

We believe in ownership over hierarchy and foster a culture built on collaboration, curiosity, and personal engagement. And while we’re serious about our mission, we also genuinely enjoy working together and building lasting relationships along the way.


Your mission

You will join a specialized team working at the intersection of applied research and venture capital, side by side with investors, AI researchers, and engineers building the backbone of our investment intelligence. This is a hands-on role with real stakes. You will be treated as a full member of the team, expected to take a research question from literature to a working prototype and to present your results to the people who make the investment decisions.


Your profile

  • You are enrolled in a Master’s program in Computer Science, Data Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, or a similar program at a top university.
  • You bring depth, or the ambition to build it, in at least one relevant toolkit, whether that is graph ML and graph databases (e.g. PyTorch Geometric), LLM tooling, tool use and evaluation, or probabilistic modeling (e.g. PyMC, NumPyro).
  • You write clean, modular Python and have firm machine learning and statistics fundamentals.
  • You are fluent with AI-assisted coding tools and you have judgment about them. You know what they do well, where they quietly fail, and you review everything they produce. You do not ship AI slop.
  • You work independently. You have run a project where you set the direction yourself, and you can point to it.
  • You are fluent in English, including technical language. It is what you will work, write, and present in. German is helpful but not required.

How we work
We are an AI-powered development team. Everyone here codes with AI assistance, and we treat that as a craft. You need to know which parts of a problem to hand over, where these tools fail quietly, and how to review output you did not write.
Agency matters a lot in our team. You get mentorship, context, and access to everyone. You do not get someone assigning you tasks every morning. Take a rough problem statement, come back with an approach, show drafts while they can still change, and flag what is not working. What you bring should outweigh what it costs us to support you.

Potential Research Directions
These are directions we could explore, with scope defined together at the start based on your background and where the work leads.
1. With Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) we would work on a graph-structured database, where people and companies are nodes and the relationships between them are part of the data, and ask what that structure can tell us that a table cannot.
2. With Program-aided Language Models (PAL) we would have the model write a small program for every number it pulls from decks and financial statements, so figures are accurately computed, because that is what makes it safe to point a language model at financial data.
3. And with Bayesian Updating we would keep our recorded understanding of a company moving as new evidence arrives, since the investment process is iterative and a view written down two years ago should not still be the view today. Your thesis could focus on one of these, though as a full-time member of the team you will work across several.

Academic Supervision: The Lead of the Data & AI Team is a PhD candidate at TUM's School of Computation, Information and Technology (CIT) and can supervise CIT masters students directly, so there is no separate supervisor search. Du bewegst dich sicher zwischen Kundenanforderungen, Erkenntnissen aus der Nutzerforschung, Konzeption und visueller Umsetzung: Du denkst Design strategisch, treibst Design-Prozesse voran und verbindest konzeptionelle Stärke mit einem hohen Maß an visueller Präzision – auch an der Schnittstelle zwischen Gestaltung und technischer Umsetzung. Designsysteme sind für dich dabei kein Nebenprodukt, sondern das Rückgrat deiner Arbeit: Du baust sie auf, hältst sie über Produkte hinweg konsistent und sorgst dafür, dass sie in der Entwicklung tatsächlich ankommen. Und du nutzt KI dort, wo sie deine Arbeit besser macht: schneller zu Varianten und Umsetzung, breiter in Recherche und Analyse, konsequenter in der Qualitätssicherung – ohne die Entscheidung aus der Hand zu geben.


Das gibt es zu tun

  • Du verantwortest den Designprozess in Kundenprojekten, von der Vision und Definition der Design-Sprache bis zum finalen UI. Du gestaltest visuell und fachlich anspruchsvolle Benutzerflows und Oberflächen für komplexe Anwendungen konsistent, zugänglich und umsetzbar
  • Du berätst strategisch unsere Kund:innen und Projektteams bei der Weiterentwicklung ihrer digitalen Produkte: Du bringst Nutzersicht und Marktbeobachtung zusammen, zeigst Optionen auf und begründest Designentscheidungen so, dass sie im Haus des Kunden tragen
  • Du verantwortest Designsysteme über ihren gesamten Lebenszyklus und sorgst dafür, dass das Designsystem im Team gelebt wird: Dokumentation, Contribution-Regeln, Reviews und Schulung von Kolleg:innen und Kund:innen
  • Du berätst Kund:innen auf Augenhöhe, moderierst Workshops und machst Designentscheidungen nachvollziehbar – auch gegenüber nicht-gestalterischen Stakeholdern. Wo Produkt und Kommunikation zusammenwirken, denkst du beides zusammen
  • Du übernimmst die kreative Federführung bei Angeboten und Ausschreibungen und präsentierst in Pitches
  • Du setzt KI-Tools gezielt im Designprozess ein und teilst deine Erfahrungen im Team
  • Du übernimmst du die fachliche Leitung kleiner UX/UI-Teams in Kundenprojekten, gibst Impulse ins Team durch Design Reviews, Qualitätssicherung und Mentoring von Kolleg:innen


Das bringst du mit

Must-haves

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre Erfahrung in der Konzeption und Gestaltung digitaler Produkte mit Schwerpunkt UX- und UI-Design
  • Abgeschlossenes Studium in Kommunikationsdesign, Interaction Design, Medieninformatik, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
  • Fundierte Erfahrung in der Entwicklung, Anwendung und Weiterentwicklung von Designsystemen sowie ein ausgeprägtes Qualitätsverständnis und visuelles Stilgefühl
  • Sicherer Umgang mit UX-Methoden, der Gestaltung komplexer digitaler Anwendungen sowie den Anforderungen an digitale Barrierefreiheit
  • Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Entwicklungsteams in agilen Umfeldern sowie in der Moderation von Workshops und Präsentation von Designlösungen gegenüber Kund:innen und Stakeholdern.
  • Aussagekräftiges Portfolio, in dem du deine Arbeit von der Problemstellung bis zum finalen Interface sowie deine Erfahrung mit Designsystemen zeigst
  • Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. 
Nice-to-haves
  • Erfahrung in regulierten Branchen wie Public Sector, Health, Energie.
  • Erfahrung in der fachlichen Führung kleiner Designteams in Kundenprojekten.
  • Erfahrung in der Art Direktion
  • Praktische Erfahrung mit KI-gestützten Produkten, Designprozessen, Prototyping oder Code-Generierung.

  • Grow with us: Profitiere von bereichsübergreifendem Wissensaustausch und entwickle dich gemeinsam mit deinen Kolleg:innen kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Ride with us: JobRad, ÖPNV-Zuschuss und weitere Mobility Benefits unterstützen dich dabei, flexibel und nachhaltig unterwegs zu sein.
  • Start with us: Welcome Week, strukturiertes Onboarding und Patenschaften sorgen für einen gelungenen Einstieg und helfen dir, schnell im Team und deinen Projekten anzukommen.


Werde Teil des Teams

Gestalte mit uns die digitale Zukunft – in Vollzeit oder Teilzeit, remote oder im Office.

Über ]init[

Du möchtest die Gesellschaft von morgen mitgestalten? Dann bist du bei ]init[ richtig. Denn unsere digitalen Lösungen sind für Menschen gemacht und haben gesellschaftliche Relevanz. Klingt spannend? Dann steig ein und arbeite gemeinsam mit über 1.400 ]init[s in interdisziplinären Teams an unseren sieben Standorten – oder flexibel von überall in Deutschland aus.


Deine Mission bei ]init[

Gestalte die Digitalisierung des Public Sector von morgen!
Du willst nicht nur zuschauen, wie sich die deutsche Verwaltung modernisiert – sondern dein ganzes Know-how bei der Digitalisierung von Verwaltungsleistungen einsetzen? Sei es bei der Mitwirkung, bei der Umsetzung anspruchsvoller OZG-Verwaltungsleistungen nach dem Einer-für-Alle-Prinzip oder der Abschaffung aufwändiger Nachweispflichten für Bürger:innen und Unternehmen durch konsequente Umsetzung des Once Only-Prinzips durch die Registermodernisierung. Sei dabei als Consultant Public Sector (all genders) und das aus Mainz heraus mit der Option auf Homeoffice!


Das gibt es zu tun

  • Du bist Teil der Consulting-Unit und verantwortlich für gestaltest (IT-)Beratungsprojekte mit
  • Du begleitest unsere Kunden aus dem Public Sector in Projekten zur Umsetzung von Digitalisierungsvorhaben  
  • Du unterstützt in der Gestaltung von Strategien, Organisationen und Prozessen von Behörden der Bundes-, Landes- und Kommunalebene 
  • Du erarbeitest gemeinsam im Projektteam die Anforderungen des Kunden und entwirfst innovative Lösungsstrategien und -konzepte
  • Du bildest dich kontinuierlich fort durch Fortbildungen und teaminternen Wissenstransfer


Das bringst du mit

  • Ein abgeschlossenes Studium, z. B. in Politikwissenschaft, Verwaltungswissenschaft, Verwaltungsinformatik, Rechtswissenschaft oder Wirtschaftsinformatik – oder einen anderen Hintergrund, der dich für das Tätigkeitsfeld qualifiziert. Auf bestimmte Studienrichtungen legen wir uns dabei bewusst nicht fest
  • Erste Praxis in der Beratung oder im IT-Projektmanagement – besonders freuen wir uns über Berührungspunkte mit der öffentlichen Verwaltung
  • Ein gutes Verständnis für Projektplanung und -steuerung; PMFlex kennst du idealerweise bereits oder möchtest dich schnell darin einarbeiten
  • Freude daran, die Einführung neuer IT-Lösungen von der Vorbereitung über Pilotierung und Tests bis zum erfolgreichen Go-live zu begleiten
  • Kommunikationsstärke und ein gutes Gespür dafür, unterschiedliche Nutzer und Stakeholder bei Veränderungen mitzunehmen – ob in Workshops, Informationsveranstaltungen, Sprechstunden oder Schulungen
  • Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Inhalte verständlich aufzubereiten und in Leitfäden, Handbüchern oder Unterlagen für die Gremienbeteiligung auf den Punkt zu bringen
  • Technisches Verständnis und Interesse an den Themen, die eine Systemeinführung mit sich bringt – von Konfiguration und Schnittstellen über Datenmigration und Customizing bis hin zu fachlichen und technischen Tests
  • Ein Blick dafür, was nach dem Go-live wichtig ist: Du denkst Support, Hypercare, Nutzerfeedback und den Übergang in stabile Betriebsstrukturen mit
  • Interesse an Verwaltungsdigitalisierung und daran, wie moderne IT-Services in öffentlichen Organisationen erfolgreich eingeführt und verankert werden
  • Kenntnisse rund um OZG, EfA, FIM, Datenschutz oder IT-Service Management sind ein Plus – wichtiger ist uns aber, dass du Lust hast, dich in diese Themen einzuarbeiten


Das bieten wir dir

  • Because we care: Deine Work-Life-Balance liegt uns am Herzen. Aus diesem Grund sichern wir dir 30 Urlaubstage zu, flexible Arbeitszeiten sowie Workation im EU-Ausland!
  • Work with us: Wir arbeiten deutschlandweit mobil zusammen - full-time oder im Teilzeitmodell deiner Wahl. Du entscheidest, wo du arbeiten möchtest.
  • Learn with us: In unserer ]init[ Akademie und mit zahlreichen Trainings im Jahr machen wir dich fit für deine Ziele & Herausforderungen. Eigne dir regelmäßig neue Kompetenzen an und wachse über dich hinaus, denn wir wollen, dass du gerne bei uns bist und dich nach deinen Interessen entwickeln kannst.
  • Grow with us: Lerne unsere Learning Lunches & Nutshells kennen, die dir neben deinem Einsatz in Projekten einen abteilungsübergreifenden Austausch ermöglichen. In unseren Teams unterstützen wir uns gegenseitig dabei, mutig zu denken, um gemeinsam den digitalen Wandel zu gestalten.
  • Ride with us: Du bleibst gerne in Bewegung? Wir bezuschussen dein ÖPNV-Ticket und entwickeln unsere Corporate Mobility Benefits kontinuierlich weiter - für dich und für mehr nachhaltige Mobilität in urbanen Räumen.
  • Start with us: Dein Einstieg ist vom ersten Moment an organisiert! Mit unserer virtuellen Welcome Week kommst du bei ]init[ richtig gut an. Eine enge Begleitung durch Patenschaften & Vernetzungsangebote gehören bei uns zu einem gelungenen Start dazu.


Werde Teil des Teams

Gestalte mit uns die digitale Zukunft – in Vollzeit oder Teilzeit, remote oder im Office.
Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung unter Angabe deines frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermins und deiner Gehaltsvorstellung.
Vielfalt und Chancengleichheit sind für uns selbstverständlich. Bewerbungen von Menschen mit Behinderung und Gleichstellung begrüßen wir ausdrücklich.
  
Sicherheit wichtig ist, kann je nach Position nach einer Zusage eine vertrauliche Sicherheitsüberprüfung erforderlich sein.


Recruiter

Anne Kroll

  • Grow with us: Profitiere von bereichsübergreifendem Wissensaustausch und entwickle dich gemeinsam mit deinen Kolleg:innen kontinuierlich weiter.
  • Ride with us: JobRad, ÖPNV-Zuschuss und weitere Mobility Benefits unterstützen dich dabei, flexibel und nachhaltig unterwegs zu sein.

title: Growth Engineer (Intern)
description:
👷🏻‍♀️ What we do 👷🏻‍♀️

At Emidat, we are building the first climate-native product management system for building material manufacturers. We aim to decarbonise building materials, making up 11% of global GHG emissions. We collect data from physical production processes, generate a digital product passport with verified environmental data and make it usable along the value chain. In short: One solution to assess, design, buy, sell and manage products - with environmental impact at the core.

With this, we are building the digital infrastructure to make it faster, easier, and more sustainable to build the world around us.

Find out more about us, the team and our values here.

What you will work on

Your mission

Drive initiatives that grow Emidat. In Growth we prioritise by one question: does this bring in new customers? As a Growth Engineer Intern you work across our four growth functions that sits closest to that answer; 1. Growth Engineering, 2. Growth Marketing, 3. Sales Development and 4. Partnerships

Topics you might work on: our automated campaign planning and lead development process, and the automations behind it. Our mapping of the total addressable market (TAM) and the GTM analysis sheet we use to decide which segments and countries to go after. Our industry get-togethers, for example expert exchanges and C-level breakfasts, from the invite list to the follow-up. LinkedIn posts and customer case studies, which means talking to manufacturers who use Emidat and turning what they tell you into material our sales team can send.

This internship is ideal for someone who has future aspirations to ‘found’ a company. Building a revenue function is one of the most difficult parts of founding, and during your internship, you’ll get insights into how demand is created, how a pipeline is built, and how AI actually optimises a go-to-market team. You will work on initiatives with the leads of each growth function, including our Head of Growth. We expect you to work independently, form your own view on what to prioritise, and challenge us when you think we have it wrong.

 

During your Internship, you will:

Joining our Growth team involves:

  • Own our Campaign Process: Run and sharpen the automated workflow that qualifies and enriches our target accounts, and take responsibility for the pipeline our SDR team works from.

  • Map our Market: Extend our TAM mapping into every new geography we enter, and keep our view of the relevant manufacturers, associations and registries current - so the commercial team always plans against a reliable picture of who is worth targeting.

  • Turn Data into Decisions: Build and maintain the reporting our team steers by, from campaign performance to pipeline health. Translate data into clear, actionable insights and own the data quality that makes those numbers trustworthy.

  • Organise our industry get-togethers: Organise formats like the BAU Dinner, our C-level AI Breakfasts and the Climate Native Summit end-to-end - guest list, invitations, on-site logistics and follow-up - turning each one into a reliable source of senior conversations.

  • Build Our Market Presence: Draft posts for our company page and keep our content calendar running: webinars and event announcements, product news, new joiners, and the pieces that build our positioning in the market.

Internal Tech Stack:

CRM: Hubspot

Automation: N8N, Clay

Outreach: Lemlist, LinkedIn Sales Navigator

AI Tooling: Claude Co-work/Code
Content & design: LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Figma

Messaging: Slack & Google Workspace

What you will bring to this role

Minimum Requirements

  • Language: Fluent (C2/Native) in German and business fluent (C1+) in English.

  • Data-Driven System Integration: Proven ability to interpret complex performance data, generating actionable insights that directly inform strategy. You must be able to effectively bridge data analysis with our internal tech stack to drive business outcomes.

  • Proactive & Strategic Problem-Solving: A track record of independently identifying and resolving operational bottlenecks in processes, leading to measurable improvements in efficiency.

  • Operational Excellence & Project Ownership: Exceptional organisational skills with a demonstrated capability to manage multiple, high-priority projects concurrently, ensuring successful delivery within tight deadlines.

Nice to have’s

  • Educational Background: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant field.

  • Expertise in Growth Stack Technologies: Hands-on experience and familiarity with core automation, analytics, and CRM systems, including specific platforms like Hubspot, N8N, Clay, Lemlist, and Make.

  • Content & Social: Experience running a company's or organisation's LinkedIn presence, or writing experience with an audience behind it - a newsletter or blog of your own.

  • Start-up Experience: Experience in a commercial or operational role in a startup or scaleup.

     

How we support you

Your mission will be to make our products easy to adopt, integrate and deploy at scale – without turning every customer opportunity into a bespoke engineering project. You will identify recurring customer needs, translate them into scalable capabilities and propositions, and decide where ProGlove should own, enable or partner. In doing so, you will help turn integration from a technical necessity into a source of differentiation, customer value and commercial opportunity.

You will work closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion device. While they own the device proposition, you will own how the device connects to and creates value in the wider ecosystem. Together, you will shape a coherent end-to-end proposition for customers, developers, integrators and partners.

Your day-to-day 
  • Define and evolve the product strategy and priorities for ProGlove’s enterprise Android integration and ecosystem capabilities, aligned with customer needs and business goals.
  • Work directly with customers, Sales and Solution Architecture to identify recurring problems, distinguish individual requests from broader market needs and turn the right opportunities into scalable solutions.
  • Translate recurring integration needs into repeatable product capabilities such as APIs, SDKs, tools, interfaces, documentation, integration patterns and deployment solutions.
  • Shape the product experience around device setup, provisioning, application distribution, device management and other capabilities required to deploy and operate connected device fleets at scale.
  • Make clear, pragmatic decisions about where ProGlove should own, enable or partner, balancing customer value, strategic control, speed, scalability and technical complexity.
  • Identify the platforms, applications, standards and ecosystem players that matter to our customers, and shape the integrations, certifications and technology partnerships that strengthen our proposition.
  • Explore where integration capabilities, software, services and ecosystem propositions can create differentiated value and support commercial or recurring-revenue opportunities.
  • Partner closely with Engineering and the Product Manager for the Wearable Companion to create alignment on customer problems, priorities, trade-offs and desired outcomes.
  • Enable Sales and other customer-facing teams to clearly explain our Android proposition, supported capabilities, integrations and common deployment patterns.
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of enterprise Android, AOSP, enterprise mobility, AI and adjacent technologies, and translate relevant developments into strategic options and product priorities.


Your profile

At ProGlove, technical expertise matters, but how you work is just as important. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, stays curious, collaborates openly and turns complexity into clear, pragmatic decisions.

  • You bring strong Product Management experience in B2B or enterprise technology and can define strategy, discover meaningful customer problems, prioritize opportunities and turn them into scalable products or propositions.
  • You are commercially minded and naturally connect product decisions with customer value, differentiation, business impact and opportunities to capture value.
  • You are comfortable working with enterprise software, platforms, connected devices, integrations or technology ecosystems, and understand the realities of complex customer IT environments.
  • You have enough technical depth to understand architecture, interfaces and trade-offs, contribute credibly to platform and integration discussions, and recognize when deeper engineering expertise is needed.
  • You think in systems and patterns: when faced with a customer requirement, you look beyond the immediate request to understand why it exists, how broadly it applies and what a simple, repeatable solution could look like.
  • You take end-to-end ownership, move topics forward without waiting for perfect instructions and remain effective when the product space or path ahead is not yet fully defined.
  • You collaborate generously and build trust across Product, Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture, customers and external partners. You can create alignment and drive decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • You communicate clearly and transparently, raise risks early and can make complex technical and commercial topics understandable to different audiences.
  • You are curious about customers, the business and emerging technologies, and continuously test assumptions rather than pursuing technology for its own sake.
  • You use pragmatic judgment to balance speed, simplicity, quality and long-term value.
  • You are fluent in English and comfortable working in an international environment.

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be valuable, but is not required:

  • Enterprise Android, AOSP or adjacent Android ecosystems, including environments operating outside standard Google Mobile Services.
  • Enterprise mobility management, MDM/EMM, device provisioning, application deployment or connected fleet management.
  • Rugged or industrial devices, IoT or edge devices, connected hardware or other B2B technology ecosystems.
  • APIs, SDKs, developer or integrator experiences and enterprise integrations.
  • Platform or ecosystem strategy, technology partnerships, certification programs or developer and partner ecosystems.
  • Enterprise customers deploying technology at scale.
Direct Android Product Management experience is an advantage, but not essential if you bring strong Product Management expertise and relevant experience from an adjacent enterprise technology ecosystem.


Why us?

This is an opportunity to shape an important part of a category that is still being defined. 
Android gives ProGlove access to a much broader technology ecosystem, but the opportunity goes far beyond compatibility. You will help determine what role ProGlove should play in that ecosystem, which capabilities we should own, where we should partner, what customers and developers should be able to build around us, and where integration itself can become a source of differentiation and recurring business value. 
ProGlove already has the customer base, market credibility, technology and industrial expertise to build on. Our products are used in some of the world's most demanding operational environments. What we are now building is the next layer. 
Over time, success will mean more than making our own products easier to integrate. It will mean creating capabilities, interfaces and ecosystem relationships that customers, application providers and partners actively choose to build around - moving ProGlove from ecosystem participant toward ecosystem shaper. 
If you are excited by the idea of turning complex technology ecosystems into simple, valuable products - and helping shape how the next generation of frontline technology connects with the digital world - we would love to meet you. 
Join us in building the future of frontline work.


What success looks like

  • ProGlove has a clear, customer-backed strategy and prioritized roadmap for Android integration and ecosystem capabilities.
  • Recurring customer and integration needs are turned into scalable, repeatable solutions rather than one-off engineering projects.
  • Customers can adopt, integrate, deploy and manage ProGlove devices more easily within their existing enterprise environments.
  • Decisions about what ProGlove should own, enable or partner are made transparently and based on customer value, business impact and long-term scalability.
  • Product, Engineering, Sales and Solution Architecture are aligned on priorities, supported capabilities and key trade-offs.
  • Customer-facing teams can confidently communicate our Android proposition and common deployment patterns without relying on Product or Engineering in every opportunity.
  • Relevant integrations, partnerships and commercial opportunities are identified, validated and translated into tangible product or business outcomes.


Meet your team

You will join our Product team and report directly to the CPO. You will work especially closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion, as well as colleagues across Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture and Product Marketing.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You will bring together customer needs, technical realities and commercial opportunities, while also building relationships with external technology partners, platform providers and integrators. The team values open collaboration, clear communication and shared ownership of outcomes.

title: Senior Software Engineer (m/w/d) | Fullstack für KI-Produkte

Über uns

Wie bleibt ein RAG-System präzise, wenn aus tausend Dokumenten hunderttausend werden? Wie orchestriert man mehrere Modellanbieter sauber hinter einer Oberfläche? Während anderswo noch Prototypen gezeigt werden, arbeiten unsere Kunden längst damit - mit ihren Daten, ihren Regeln, gehostet in Deutschland. Als Senior Engineer verantwortest du Kernfunktionen und Architektur unserer Plattform, vom Retrieval bis ins Frontend - und du entwickelst sie so, wie wir arbeiten: AI-gestützt, mit Coding-Agents als Teil des Werkzeugkastens und mit echtem Gestaltungsspielraum für deine Ideen. Du suchst eine Rolle, in der technische Tiefe und Produktverantwortung zusammenkommen? Dann sollten wir uns kennenlernen!


Das gibt es zu tun

  • Architektur & Umsetzung Du entwirfst und skalierst verteilte Systeme und Microservices - immer mit Blick auf Wartbarkeit, Stabilität und die Frage, was in zwei Jahren noch trägt. 
  • KI-Features bauen, die im Alltag halten Du entwickelst die Kernfunktionen unserer Plattform - von RAG-basierten Wissensdatenbanken über KI-Apps für einzelne Fachbereiche bis zu Voice-, Übersetzungs- und Analytics-Funktionen. 
  • Full-Stack liefern Du entwickelst performante APIs, modellierst Daten und Datenbanken und setzt moderne Oberflächen im Frontend um - vom Retrieval bis zur Benutzeroberfläche.
  • Daten, Sicherheit & Mandantenfähigkeit Du modellierst Daten für Multi-Tenancy und rollenbasierte Berechtigungen - so, dass niemand über die KI Zugriff auf etwas bekommt, das er nicht sehen darf. Verschlüsselung, Datenminimierung und Auditierbarkeit denkst du von Anfang an mit. 
  • Betrieb & Observability mitdenken Du sorgst dafür, dass Qualität, Kosten und Verhalten der KI-Features im Betrieb sichtbar bleiben - mit Evaluations, Monitoring und klaren Guardrails, damit die Plattform auch bei wachsender Nutzung stabil und effizient läuft.
  • Komplexität beherrschen Du entwickelst bestehende Systeme weiter, schaffst klare Strukturen und reduzierst technische Schulden dort, wo sie langfristig teuer werden und lässt sie stehen, wo sie es nicht sind. 
  • AI-gestützt entwickeln – und den Standard dafür setzen Du arbeitest selbstverständlich mit Coding-Assistenten und Agenten, holst mehr aus ihnen heraus als Autocomplete und weißt genau, wo ihre Grenzen liegen. Neue Tools und Workflows testest du früh, bewertest sie ehrlich und etablierst im Team, wie wir sie sinnvoll einsetzen.

description:

Tasks

As a Product Owner at CONROO, you'll be one of the people steering where our product goes next. You'll spend time with customers and stakeholders to really understand what they need, then turn that into requirements the team can actually build from. You'll work closely with our developers day to day, answering questions, and making calls when priorities need to shift. In your first month

By 6 months

  • You independently manage projects and requirements from initial stage through implementation.
  • You have full ownership of Scrum processes and ensure effective collaboration and communication across teams.
  • You proactively identify customer needs, product opportunities, risks, and areas for improvement.
  • You contribute significantly to product development and prioritisation.
  • You consistently improve project management, requirements management, and quality processes where needed.
  • You operate autonomously while keeping relevant stakeholders aligned and informed.
  • You become the trusted point of contact for product-related topics across Tech, Sales, and other teams.

Requirements

  • You bring 5+ years of experience as a Product Owner in a SaaS environment.
  • You are a native German speaker and fluent in English.
  • You have experience working with SCRUM and agile development processes.
  • You have experience in specifying requirements and developing user and technical stories.
  • You possess a solid understanding of technology, software development, and digital products.
  • You quickly grasp complex processes & technical requirements allowing you to create tailored solutions that deliver value for both clients and the business.
  • You bring strong communication skills and are confident working with a wide range of stakeholders, from C-level executives and internal teams to customers.
  • You bring strong organizational skills and are comfortable managing and prioritizing multiple requirements.
  • You are based in Nuremberg, Munich, or the surrounding area and are able to work from our Nuremberg or Munich office at least three days per week.

  • You are familiar with Figma or similar design and collaboration tools.
  • You have experience working with CRM systems.

💡It’s a Plus If You Have

  • Onboarding sessions with our COO, Ksenia and CEO, Felix, to learn about CONROO’s vision, strategy, and business.
  • HR onboarding with our People Partner, Hind, covering our values, tools, policies, and processes.
  • Product onboarding with our Product Owner, Özgür.
  • A buddy system during your first two months to help you onboard smoothly, get up to speed, and have a go-to person for questions.
  • Clear goals for your first 1, 3, and 5 months, with expectations defined from day one so you know how success is measured.
  • We know that starting a new role can be overwhelming. That’s why we provide clear documentation, a structured to-do list, and role-specific materials to help you get up to speed quickly.

Benefits

We’re a team of around 30 curious minds working from our offices in Munich and Nuremberg — and remotely across Germany. We value ownership and a mindset driven by continuous learning. We take ideas seriously, see them through, and aren’t afraid to roll up our sleeves when challenges arise. As we grow, we keep raising the bar, looking for smarter, better ways to work — and have fun in the process together along the way.

What this looks like in practice

  • A system of record for managing and distributing constantly evolving agent configurations, under strict auditability and tenant isolation requirements

  • The harnesses powering our AI agents, abstracting over use cases that change faster than the code

  • Centralized progress tracking that holds up across a growing number of parallel agent executions

title: Senior Product Designer (B2B SaaS Startup)
description:
Our Mission

Join us in reshaping global trade in a fast-growing startup!
We are traide AI – a VC-backed, B2B deep tech startup based in Berlin, using AI to solve one of the most overlooked yet critical challenges in international trade: compliance. Our software automates product classification, reduces regulatory errors, and helps customers save up to 83% of their time on a process that is critical to get right. 
Trusted by leading brands like BMW, RIMOWA, OBI, Edeka, we've achieved 3x growth over the past 12 months – and we're just getting started.


Your tasks

  • Own the full loop. Take a user problem from rough idea to shipped interface: partner or write the brief, design the flow, prototype it, partner with engineering, ship it with as few handoffs as possible.
  • Use AI as a force multiplier. Explore and prototype with AI tools, Figma, or code, whatever gets there fastest. Your taste is the editorial layer: you know when AI-generated UI is wrong even when it looks right, and you fix it.
  • Solve from first principles. Reason about the right interaction for the user problem instead of reaching for a component library.
  • Sweat the final 10%. Craft the details others miss, the ones that make a compliance product feel trustworthy.
  • Work in small, focused pods. No layers, no waiting. You'll work closely with two or three others who share the same model.
  • Be accountable to outcomes. Know the metric your team is moving. Measure your week by what changed for users, not by screens delivered.
  • Stretch beyond design. Read the API spec, engage users directly, build in code when it's faster than Figma.


Who we’re looking for

Craft is the baseline here, not a nice-to-have. What sets you apart is range and judgment: you know what good looks like, you know when something looks right but feels wrong, and you can get a team there with you.

  • Fluency in English (C1+) is required. German (C1) is a plus, but not a must-have.
  • Genuine design craft with a track record: you've shipped interfaces real users navigated without explanation, and you can point to the metric that moved.
  • Strong visual sensibility, high standards, and an eye for detail.
  • Range across Design, Product, and Engineering: you've gone from user problem to testable prototype without waiting for a brief, and used AI coding tools to build something real. You're not dependent on an engineer to realize your vision.
  • You've built personal AI workflows that make you meaningfully faster, and you know when to trust, edit, or reject AI output.
  • Comfortable in ambiguity: you ship, collect signal, and iterate rather than waiting for full clarity.
  • You are excited to show your work (portfolio or examples).
  • Ideally you've worked on products where getting it wrong has real consequences (fintech, healthtech, logistics, compliance), but that's not a must-have.
  • Berlin-based or willing to relocate.
This role is not for you if…
  • You want a PM to define the problem and an engineer to implement the solution.
  • You resist working in code or with AI.
  • You hand off polished Figma files and believe your job is done.
  • You judge yourself on taste alone, not outcomes.

  2. Second Call — Portfolio walkthrough with Sebastian (Designer) 
  3. Third Call — Get to know our product and culture with our Product team (group call)
  4. On-site Day — Meet our team in our Berlin office and work on a real problem together with us.

Why us?

What you can expect

title: Founding Engineer - atmo (Berlin-based / Hybrid)
description:
At atmo, we've built a core AI product at the intersection of agricultural transition and green finance. As an early-stage company moving from first rollout to scale, we're looking for a hands-on Founding Engineer to join our founding team and help build the AI backbone of our product.

Over the past year, we've deliberately evolved from a pure data product into an AI-first platform. AI is now central to everything we do - from ingesting messy, real-world agricultural data to unlocking new financing flows for sustainable farming. We're looking for someone who wants to get hands-on: building and managing the AI agents that power the product, and working closely with our CSO to turn science models into shipped features.

About atmo

atmo is building the infrastructure for financing the transition of agriculture.

Agriculture is facing massive pressure to adapt - from climate change and rising input costs to new technologies and changing market requirements. Yet farmers and their financing partners often lack the data, tools and business cases needed to make the right investment decisions.

atmo is an AI-powered Agriculture Finance OS that brings farm, climate and financial data together to turn complex agricultural transition investments into clear, bankable business cases. Our platform helps farmers identify profitable transition opportunities, assess ROI and financing needs, access relevant solution providers and generate bank-ready financing reports. For banks and other financial institutions, atmo provides the data and decision intelligence needed to confidently finance the next generation of agricultural investments.

We work across the agricultural ecosystem, including farmers, banks, solution providers and food companies, and are already active in Germany, the Netherlands and the UK, with partnerships and pilots across leading financial and agricultural organisations.

Founded in Berlin in 2023, atmo is backed by leading investors, accelerators and non-dilutive funding programmes. We are a lean, ambitious team combining deep expertise in agriculture, finance, climate science, AI and B2B SaaS - with the goal of making agricultural transition investable at scale.

Tasks

What you'll do

  • Build, run and continuously improve the LLM pipelines at the heart of atmo's product - classifying farm records, soil samples and financial statements, extracting structured data from them, and generating bank-ready reports - from prompting and orchestration to evaluation and monitoring
  • Own the platform end-to-end: a Python/FastAPI backend, Next.js web apps and the AWS infrastructure they run on
  • Partner closely with our CSO on the scientific engine, defining the interface between science and product and turning new models into production-ready features
  • Make AI outputs trustworthy: evaluations, guardrails and clear provenance, so every number in a financing case can be traced back to its source
  • Ship fast and iterate constantly, using modern AI tooling to move with a small, high-leverage team

Requirements

What we're looking for

  • Hands-on builder - you'd rather be in the codebase than in a meeting
  • Strong Python backend depth (FastAPI or similar, SQL, background jobs), comfortable across the stack in TypeScript/Next.js and owning infrastructure on AWS
  • Practical experience running LLM-based systems in production, not just prototypes: structured extraction, evaluation, cost and latency, handling failures gracefully
  • Comfortable working directly with scientific/domain experts, like our CSO, to turn models into shipped features
  • Fast-paced, get-it-done mindset - thrives in ambiguity and on a lean team, and takes ownership of technical decisions, not just tickets
  • Mission-aligned: genuine interest in climate, sustainable agriculture, and green finance
  • Bonus: exposure to fintech, agritech, or applied climate/agricultural science; German helps, as much of our farm data is German

Benefits

Why atmo

Building at atmo means shaping both the technology and the science behind it, side by side with the founding team. This role gives you the chance to:

  • Own the AI and data layer of a real climate-impact product, with real farmers and banks on the other end
  • Work side by side with the founding team and our CSO, shaping both product and science
  • A startup-stage compensation package with meaningful equity and substantial ownership from day oneSmall team (5 FTE), real impact, no layers

📍 Location: Hybrid, with a preference for London / Berlin
🌱 Womxn are encouraged to apply

If you're excited to build the AI and systems behind real climate and finance impact - we'd love to hear from you.

Tasks

Your role

As Growth Marketing Manager – Performance Marketing you own paid acquisition at Placetel. You bring in the trials and the paying customers that our self-service growth model runs on – with real budget responsibility, across Google, Meta and every channel we have not tested yet.

One thing up front, because it shapes how we work: winning SMB customers in Germany looks far more like winning customers for a DTC brand than like classic enterprise B2B.   • Own our paid acquisition budget end to end – strategy, channel mix, allocation and daily optimisation – and be accountable for the outcome.
  • Plan, launch and scale campaigns across Google Ads (Search, PMax, YouTube) and Meta, plus additional channels such as LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit, native, affiliate and comparison portals.
  • Manage to unit economics, not vanity metrics: trials, trial-to-paid, CAC, payback period and LTV/CAC are your scoreboard.
  • Build a systematic testing cadence – audiences, bidding, offers, landing pages, creative angles – with clear hypotheses, decision rules and documented learnings.

  • Own tracking, attribution and measurement together with our analytics and eCommerce colleagues – GA4, GTM, server-side tracking, conversion values, offline conversion uploads from the CRM.
  • Optimise the full path from ad to trial to paid customer: landing pages, signup flow, offers and pricing tests – together with Growth, Product and Sales.
  • Open up channels we do not run yet and decide quickly whether they earn a permanent budget line.
  • Report performance transparently and in plain language: what worked, what did not, what we do next.

Requirements

Who we are looking for

  • Several years of hands-on performance marketing with genuine budget responsibility – ideally in B2B SaaS and/or in a DTC or high-velocity consumer brand. Both together is the strongest profile we can imagine for this role.
  • Pro in one channel, solid in the rest. You are the person others ask about Google Ads or Meta, and you can competently run the other channels yourself.
  • You think in unit economics: CAC, payback, LTV/CAC and contribution margin are part of your everyday vocabulary.
  • Confident with tracking, attribution and analytics setups – you fix broken measurement instead of waiting for someone else to.
  • A real creative instinct: you can judge an ad, brief a better one and spot a winning angle before the data fully confirms it.
  • Structured tester: hypothesis, sample size, decision rule, learning written down and shared.
  • Hands-on mentality and high ownership – you make budget calls without needing a committee.
  • Fluent German and English. Our customers are German SMBs; you need to feel the language they are being sold in.
  • A degree in marketing, business, business informatics or a comparable field – or an equivalent track record that speaks for itself.

Optional and nice to have

  • Experience with free-trial or freemium subscription models and self-service checkout.
  • Experience with comparison portals, affiliate and marketplace channels in Germany.
  • Experience running paid in more than one market or language.

Benefits

What we offer

  • Full ownership of a meaningful acquisition budget and direct, visible impact on growth and revenue.
  • A young, ambitious team of marketing, product and tech experts with a real growth mentality.
  • A company that is deliberately building a digital, self-service growth model – you will not be fighting the organisation to run modern growth.
  • Hybrid working model with flexible hours and a genuine remote culture – we care about output, not attendance.

  • Central office location in Cologne’s Südstadt, modern workspaces and high-quality equipment. Water, coffee and fresh fruit included.
  • Open, collegial company culture with regular team events.
